Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:10:1.english: [They are] exempt - Because it is not known by whom he was killed.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:10:2.hebrew: שקירב מיתתו - ופלוגתייהו דרבי יהודה בן בתירא ורבנן מפ' בסנהדרין בפרק אלו הן הנשרפין (דף עח.). ר' יהודה סבר: "כי יכה כל נפש אדם" כתיב, דמשמע כל דהו נפש, ורבנן סברי: כולה נפש משמע. והיינו "הכשרתי במקצת נזקו", דומיא דחופר בור, שהראשון הזיק והאחרון הרג:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:10:2.english: That he hastened his death - And the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira and the Rabbis is explained in Sanhedrin, in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Hen HaNisrafin (78a). Rabbi Yehuda holds: "When [one] smites any [kol] human life" is written, which implies any [amount of] life; whereas the Rabbis hold: It implies an entire life. And this is [an example of] "I facilitated part of its damage," similar to one who digs a pit [and another deepens it], where the first one caused damage and the last one killed.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:12:1.english: Not in accordance with Rabbi, and in accordance with the Rabbis we establish [it] - For the halakha is in accordance with the majority.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:13:1.english: It does not teach "for its damage" - So that it would imply that he must pay [for] a whole, live ox, and he [the damager] takes the carcass.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:13:2.hebrew: אלא בתשלומי נזקו - דמשמע השלמה, שיטול ניזק את הנבילה, וזה משלים לו מה שפחתתו מיתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:13:2.english: Rather, "for the payments of its damage" - For it implies completion, [namely,] that the injured party takes the carcass, and this [damager] completes for him what death diminished it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:14:1.hebrew: תשלומי נזקו מלמד כו' - לשון השלמה, משלים לו לניזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:14:1.english: Payments for his damage teaches, etc. - [It is] an expression of completion; [the damager] completes [what is lacking] for the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:14:2.hebrew: הבעלים מטפלין בנבילה - כלומר, נוטלין את הנבילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:14:2.english: The owners attend to the carcass - That is to say, they take the carcass.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:15:1.english: Yashlimenna [he shall complete it] - [This] implies that he shall pay the remainder.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:16:1.hebrew: יביאהו עד - דריש השתא הכי: "אם טרוף יטרף" השור בפשיעתו של שומר שכר — דהאי קרא בשומר שכר כתיב, כדאמרינן בהשואל (ב"מ דף צד:) פרשה שנייה נאמרה בשומר שכר — "יביאהו עד הטרפה", ישלם כל ההיזק עד דמי הטרפה, אבל דמי הטריפה עצמה לא ישלם, דניזק מטפל וטורח בנבילה למוכרה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:16:1.english: Let him bring a witness [yevi’ehu ed] - He expounds [the verse] now thus: "If [it] be torn in pieces," [meaning] the ox, through the negligence of a paid bailee — for this verse is written regarding a paid bailee, as we say in [chapter] HaShoel (Bava Metzia 94b) [that] the second section was stated regarding a paid bailee — "let him bring it until [ad] the torn animal," [meaning] he shall pay all the damage up to the value of the torn animal, but the value of the torn animal itself he shall not pay, for the injured party attends to and troubles himself with the carcass to sell it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:17:1.hebrew: לניזק - שיטלנו בדמים, ועליו ישלים המזיק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:17:1.english: To the injured [party] - That [the injured party] takes it at [its] monetary value, and upon it the damager completes [the payment].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:1:1.hebrew: פשיטא - ולמה הוה לן למיתנייה? הרי הראשון לא סייע כלום, דכל מה דשביק ליה מעמיא ואזיל. אבל חופר בור תשעה, רוב מיתתו הוא עושה, אלא האחרון מקרבה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:1:1.english: It is obvious - And why would we need to teach it? After all, the first one did not assist at all, since whatever [fire] he left was dying down and going out. By contrast, one who digs a pit [of] nine [handbreadths] causes most of its lethality; rather, the last one brings it closer.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:20:1.hebrew: אי ס"ד נבילה דמזיק - והאי "המת יהיה לו" למזיק קאמר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:20:1.english: If it enters your mind [that] the carcass [belongs] to the damager - and this [phrase], "the dead [animal] shall be his," refers to the damager.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:20:2.hebrew: ולשתוק - קרא מיניה, דלא אצטריך להכי, דפשיטא לן כיון דשלם "שור תחת השור", נבילה שלו היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:20:2.english: And be silent - [Let] the verse [be silent] regarding it, for it is not needed for this, since it is obvious to us [that] once he paid "an ox for the ox," the carcass is his [the damager's].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:21:1.hebrew: מכה בהמה לא שכיחא - שיהא אדם מזיק בהמה של חבירו, לפיכך לא החמיר עליו הכתוב לטרוח במכירת הנבילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:21:1.english: [The case of] "One who strikes an animal" is uncommon - for a person to damage his fellow's animal; therefore, Scripture was not stringent upon him to trouble [himself] with the sale of the carcass.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:22:1.hebrew: טריפה דממילא - שהזאב טרפה והשומר לא נתכוון, אמטו להכי חס רחמנא עליה דלא למיטרח בנבילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:22:1.english: A torn animal, [which happened] by itself - For a wolf tore it and the bailee did not intend [for this to happen]; therefore, the Merciful One had compassion on him, [so that he would] not have to trouble himself with the carcass.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:22:2.hebrew: דבידים - קא מזיק. אימא על המזיק לטרוח בנבילה ומשלם הדמים, קמ"ל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:22:2.english: With [his] hands - [i.e.,] he causes damage [directly]. I might say [that it is] upon the damager to trouble himself with the carcass and he pays the [full] value; [therefore] it teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:23:1.hebrew: והמת יהיה לו - משתעי בשור נגח דשכיח, ובידים הוא ממש, (שהשור) שהוא (ממונו של מזיק) נתכוין להזיק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:23:1.english: And the carcass shall be his - [This] speaks of a goring ox, which is common, and it is literally [like] by hand, ([for] the ox), which is (the damager's property), intended to cause damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:24:1.hebrew: שומר שכר - שפשע ונטרפה על ידי זאב, כנזקי גופו חשיב ליה, שהרי היה עליו לשומרה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:24:1.english: A paid bailee - Who was negligent and [the animal] was torn by a wolf: [the Gemara] considers it like damage [caused] by his own body, since it was incumbent upon him to guard it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:26:1.hebrew: השתא אי הוו ליה טריפות - למזיק כשיעור כל דמי נזקו, הוה יהיב ליה בעל כרחיה דניזק, דאמר מר: "ישיב" — לרבות כו', דידיה מיבעיא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:26:1.english: Now, if he had torn [animal] carcasses - [That is, if] the damager [had them] to the amount of the entire value of his damage, he could give [them] to him against the injured party's will, as the Master said: "He shall recompense" — to include [items worth money], etc.; is his [own carcass] necessary [to be stated]?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:27:1.english: It is only necessary - [referring to] that which Scripture wrote, that the injured party deals with the carcass.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:27:2.hebrew: אלא לפחת נבילה - דהכי אמר רחמנא, דמשעת מיתה קאי ברשותיה דניזק, ואם הסריח ופחתה דמים משעת מיתה ועד שעת העמדה בדין, פסידא דניזק הוא. ומשלם ליה מזיק מה שהנזק הוי יתר על הדמים שהיתה נבילה שוה בשעת מיתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:27:2.english: Only for the diminishing [value] of the carcass - For thus the Merciful One said, that from the time of death [the carcass] stands in the domain of the injured party, and if it putrefied and decreased in value from the time of death until the time of standing in judgment, the loss is the injured party's. And the damager pays him [only] the amount by which the [original value of the] damaged [animal] exceeds the value that the carcass was worth at the time of death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:2:1.english: Such as Pappa bar Abba - For he was a heavy man.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:3:1.hebrew: פשיטא - דלא דמי לבור, שהראשון גרם נזקין והרג חציו או רובו, אלא משום הכי הוא דמפטר, דאמר ליה: אי לאו אתה, הוה מתזיק ולא הוה מיית; אבל אלו לא שברו כלום כל זמן שלא בא זה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:3:1.english: [It is] obvious - For it is not similar to a pit, where the first [digger] caused damage and killed half of it or most of it, [and] it is only for this reason that he is exempt [from liability for its death], for he says to him: "If not for you, [the animal] would have been injured and would not have died"; whereas these [first five people] broke nothing at all as long as this [last] one had not come.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:4:2.hebrew: היכא מיתרצא - הואיל ומותבת הכי. אבל מוסר שורו ומרבה בחבילות לא מתנייתא נינהו, אלא מסברא הוו מקשי להו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:4:2.english: How is [the baraita] explained - Since you object thus. However, [the cases of] one who hands over his ox and one who adds bundles are not baraitot; rather, they were raising them [as objections] from logical reasoning.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:5:1.hebrew: דבלאו איהו הוה מיתבר בתרי שעי - ולהכי אצטריך למיתנייה לאשמועינן דאפי' הכי חייב. ומיהו בהדי ההיא דחופר בור לא מצי למיתנייה דתהוי הך כהכשר במקצת נזקו דמתני', דהאי לא מקצת נזק הוא אלא כל נזק, שהראשונים לא התחילו לשברן, כי היכי דחופר בור ט' הזיקתו הבל חום של ט' והבל חום של י' הרגו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:5:1.english: Where without him it would have broken in two hours - And for this [reason] it was necessary to teach it, to inform us that even so he is liable. However, alongside that [case] of one who digs a pit, [the Tanna] could not teach it, such that this would be like "preparing part of its damage" of our Mishnah; for this is not partial damage, rather the entire damage, since the first ones did not begin to break it — just as [in the case of] one who digs a pit of nine [handbreadths], the heat-vapor of nine damaged it, and the heat-vapor of ten killed it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:6:1.hebrew: ולימא להו אי לאו אתון בדידי - לחוד לא הוה מיתבר, ואתם כשישבתי היה לכם לעמוד, ומדלא עמדתם — אתם כמוני שברתם. וגבי משלים בור לעשרה ליכא לאקשויי הכי, דמאי הוה ליה לקמא למיעבד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:6:1.english: And let him say to them: Were it not for you, by myself - alone it would not have broken; and you, when I sat down, should have stood up, and since you did not stand up, you broke [it] just like me. And regarding one who completes a pit to ten [handbreadths], one cannot raise this difficulty, for what could the first [person] have done?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:7:1.hebrew: לא צריכא דבהדי דסמיך עלייהו - לעולם דבלאו איהו לא הוה מיתבר כלל. ודקאמרת "פשיטא", לא צריכא דלא ישב עליו, אלא עמד על רגליו ונסמך עליהם, ואתא לאשמועינן דכחו כגופו דמי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:7:1.english: No, it is necessary [where] as he was leaning upon them - In fact, [it is a case] where without him it would not have broken at all. And [as for] what you said, "[It is] obvious" — no, it is necessary [for a case] where he did not sit upon it, rather he stood on his feet and leaned upon them, and [the Gemara] comes to teach us that his force is like his body.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:7:2.hebrew: סמך בהו - נסמך עליהם ולא יכלו לעמוד. לישנא אחרינא, דזגא מזגא גרסינן, כדאמרינן בעלמא: חזי למיזגא עליה (שבת דף מח.):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 10b:7:2.english: He leaned upon them - He leaned upon them, and they could not stand. Another version: we read [the text as] "dezaga mezaga" [leaning], as we say elsewhere: "[It is] fit for reclining upon" (Shabbat 48a).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:10:1.hebrew: כולן פטורין - וביש לראשון כדי להמית, דבשאין בו כדי להמית אפילו לרבנן אחרון חייב, כדמוכח בפ' כל הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עח.):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:10:1.english: They are all exempt - And [this applies] where the first [person's blow] has enough [force] to kill, for where it does not have enough [force] to kill, even according to the Rabbis the last [one] is liable, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Kol Hanisrafin (Sanhedrin 78a).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:15:1.hebrew: ישלימנה - "בעל הבור ישלם" — אין לדרוש "ישלם" "ישלים", אבל "ישלמנה" משמע שהבהמה עצמה ישלם, וזה אי אפשר שכבר מתה; לפיכך יש לדרוש "ישלימנה":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:15:1.english: Yashlimenna [he shall complete it] - [Regarding the verse] "The owner of the pit shall pay [yeshalem]," one cannot expound yeshalem [as] yashlim [he shall complete]; however, yeshalmennah ["he shall pay it"] implies that he shall pay the animal itself, and this is impossible, since it has already died; therefore, one must expound [it as] yashlimenna [he shall complete it].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:16:1.hebrew: לא ישלם - אע"ג דקרא בשומר שכר כתיב, דפטור מאונסין, מ"מ מדכתיב "עד הטרפה לא ישלם", יש ללמוד דהיכא דישלם, לא ישלם כלום בשביל הטרפה עצמה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:16:1.english: He shall not pay - Even though the verse is written regarding a paid bailee, who is exempt from [liability for] unavoidable accidents, nevertheless, since it is written, "[up] until the torn animal he shall not pay," one can derive that where he does pay, he shall not pay anything for the torn animal itself.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:23:1.hebrew: הא משום דממילא כו' - כלומר: מחד מינייהו לא אתיא, אבל מתרוייהו אתיא במה הצד; ולא חש להאריך ולדקדק בזה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:23:1.english: "And that [one] because [it occurred] by itself," etc. - That is to say: from either one of them [alone] it cannot be derived, whereas from both of them [together] it can be derived through a mah hatzad [common characteristic]; and [the Gemara] did not bother to elaborate and be precise about this.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:27:1.hebrew: לא נצרכא אלא לפחת נבילה - אע"ג דבפ' המניח (לקמן בבא קמא לד.) אמרינן כיחשה כשעת העמדה בדין, משום דקרנא דתורא קבירא בי' — התם משום דלא מתה, ויש לו להמתין עד שתתרפא; אבל הכא, מיד היה לו למוכרה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:27:1.english: [It] is necessary only for the diminishing [value] of the carcass - Even though in the chapter [entitled] HaManiach (below, Bava Kamma 34a) we say [that if the injured animal] became lean, [its assessment is] as of the time of standing in court, because the horn of the ox is buried in it — there [it is] because it did not die, and he must wait until it heals; but here, he should have sold it immediately.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:2:1.hebrew: כגון פפא בר אבא - מפרש רשב"ם דנקט פפא בר אבא לפי שלסתם בני אדם הוא שאול לכל הבא מאיליו לישב עליה, כי סתם ספסל עשוי לכך, והוי כמתה מחמת מלאכה; אבל פפא בר אבא, שהוא משונה וכבד משאר בני אדם, סתמא אין שאול לו. ולפי' צ"ל: "כגון פפא בר אבא" אכולהו קאי, מדקאמר בסמוך דא"ל: "אי לאו את, הוה יתבינן פורתא וקיימין" — משמע דאם היה נשבר היו חייבין. ומיהו לפי המסקנא, דמשני דבהדי דקסמך עלייהו, אין צריך לפרש דחייב אלא אחרון בלבד; ומתוך כך פטר ארבעה בני אדם שישבו על ספסל אחד של אלמנה ושברוהו, והר"ר עזריאל חייב לשלם. ור"ת מפרש דנקט פפא בר אבא משום דקאמר במסקנא דכחו כגופו דמי, ודוקא פפא בר אבא, שהוא אדם כבד ומתוך כבדו מונען לעמוד; אבל שאר בני אדם, שאין כבידין כל כך ואין סמיכתן מעכב מלעמוד, אינהו נמי פשעו שלא עמדו, וכולן חייבין. ולפי זה צריך לומר דרב פפא עצמו בא לתרץ מה שהקשה "ותו ליכא":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:2:1.english: Such as Pappa bar Abba - Rashbam explains that [the Gemara] mentions Pappa bar Abba because for ordinary people, it [a bench] is [considered] borrowed for anyone who comes on his own to sit upon it, since an ordinary bench is made for this, and [if it breaks] it is like [an animal that] died because of its work; however, [for] Pappa bar Abba, who is unusual and heavier than other people, it is ordinarily not borrowed for him. Therefore, one must say [that] "such as Pappa bar Abba" refers to all of them, from the fact that [the Gemara] says shortly thereafter that they say to him: "Were it not for you, we would have sat a little longer and stood up" — implying that if it had broken [under them alone], they would have been liable. However, according to the conclusion, where [the Gemara] answers that [it broke] instantaneously as he leaned upon them, one need only explain that the last one alone is liable; and on this basis, [Rashbam] exempted four people who sat on a widow's bench and broke it, whereas Rabbi Azriel obligated [them] to pay. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that [Rav Pappa] mentioned Pappa bar Abba because [the Gemara] says in the conclusion that his force is like his body, and [this applies] specifically [to] Pappa bar Abba, who is a heavy person and through his heaviness prevents them from standing up; but other people, who are not so heavy and whose leaning does not prevent [the others] from standing up, they too were negligent in that they did not stand up, and all of them are liable. And according to this, one must say that Rav Pappa himself came to resolve what he had objected, "And are there no more?"

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:3:1.hebrew: מאי קעביד - בכולה שמעתין צ"ל: "מאי קעביד טפי מאחריני, וישלם כל אחד חלקו?" ואין לומר דליפטר, דתניא פרק הפרה (לקמן בבא קמא נא.): "אחד החוקק בור לי', ובא אחר והשלימו לעשרים, ובא אחר והשלימו לשלשים — כולם חייבין", אע"ג דבלאו איהו הוה מתה. מיהו, בזה צריך לדקדק: וכי בשביל שהשליך איש עץ בתוך אש גדולה יתחייב? הא לא דמי אלא לאחד שחופר בור י' ובא אחר והשלימו לי"א:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 10b:3:1.english: What did he do - Throughout this entire sugya, [the Gemara] means to say: "What did he do more than the others [such that he alone should pay], and [instead] each one should pay his share?" And one cannot say that he should be exempt [entirely], for it is taught in a baraita in chapter HaParah (below, Bava Kamma 51a): "If one digs a pit to [a depth of] ten [handbreadths], and another comes and completes it to twenty, and another comes and completes it to thirty — they are all liable," even though without him [the last one, the animal] would have died. However, regarding this [baraita] one must examine closely: Would a person be liable merely because he threw a piece of wood into a large fire?! [Surely] this is only comparable to one who digs a pit of ten [handbreadths] and another comes and completes it to eleven.
